Communication style only: no tools, commands, network or file writes. It explicitly keeps full prose for security warnings, irreversible actions, step-order-sensitive instructions, questions to the user, and anything persisted (code, comments, commits, docs, PRs, memory files).

name: Ponytail
description: "Lazy senior dev" mode: the smallest complete change, reuse before adding code or dependencies, no unrequested abstractions; ends each reply with what was skipped or not checked. Levels lite/full/ultra.
author: DietrichGebert

review.reviewer: Claude (ES11.1: full read of the skill folder at the pinned revision; automated scan; plugin, hook and installer layers inspected but excluded)
review.approvedBy: Owner — ES11.2 approval authorization (2026-10-27); core skill folder only
findings: Automated scan: 1 file (SKILL.md), 0 scripts, no pattern hits.

Changes execution behavior, not just tone: it decides what code gets written (smallest complete change, reuse, no new dependencies or abstractions) and writes "shortcut: <limit>, <when to upgrade>" comments into code.

Guardrails are explicit: "Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, ... anything the user asked for"; finish callers, tests and fixtures the change breaks; new non-trivial logic needs a small test or assert; moved code keeps its error handling.

Weak spots: trivial changes need no test; tests are "one small test or assert" and the skill never says to run them; "ultra" pushes back on requested scope. Pair with verification-before-completion so completion claims still need fresh evidence.
Broad and persistent: "Use on any coding task" plus "active for the whole session" means it will trigger often once activated and overrides default engineering style until "stop ponytail".

Plugin-only and excluded: session/subagent hooks that run Node, a default-on per-turn ledger written to ~/.config/ponytail/band/<project>.csv, an optional per-turn webhook, statusline scripts, and always-on rules files for about ten agents (AGENTS.md, .agents/rules, .cursor/rules, ...).

Overlap: complementary to verification-before-completion (Ponytail reports what it skipped; VBC requires evidence); "ultra" partly overlaps grilling (challenging scope); its minimal-documentation stance can pull against writing-plans' detailed plan template. Upstream ponytail-review/ponytail-audit overlap requesting-code-review and the security skills and were not registered.
review.notes: Approved in ES11.2 for the core skills/ponytail folder only, at the pinned revision and content hash. Not approved: ponytail-review/ponytail-audit, hooks, the ledger/telemetry, the webhook, statusline scripts and always-on rules files. Approval is not agent verification: coding behavior is unevaluated, it does not require running tests, and its broad "any coding task" trigger may be unwanted in some projects. Medium behavioral risk; before activating, evaluate it like ES8 (treatment vs control) and pair it with verification-before-completion; activate per project only.
